faq.q: Is there a cost for your guidance?
faq.a: There is no fee for our guidance. We are compensated by the carriers whose plans we place, and the premium for a given plan is the same whether you enroll through us or directly.

faq.q: What does it mean that King Health is independent?
faq.a: We are not employed by a single insurance company. We represent multiple carriers, which allows us to compare plans side by side and recommend the one that fits your circumstances and your budget rather than a sales quota.

faq.q: Which states do you serve?
faq.a: King Health is licensed in New Jersey and North Carolina, so we can advise and place coverage for residents of either state. Conversations can take place by phone or at our office in Newark.

faq.q: What happens after we submit this form?
faq.a: We review your request and reach out personally to arrange a conversation at a time that suits you. Submitting the form is a request to be contacted rather than an application for coverage, and it carries no obligation.

senior-benefits.title: Senior Benefits | King Health
senior-benefits.heading: Senior benefits that bring clarity to the years ahead
senior-benefits.lede: We guide you through Medicare, final expense coverage and supplemental benefits with patience, so that every decision feels clear and every plan fits your budget.
senior-benefits.card_text: Medicare guidance, final expense coverage and supplemental benefits arranged with patience and explained in plain language.
overview: Approaching Medicare is a meaningful milestone, and the choices that come with it deserve calm, careful attention. We help you understand how Original Medicare, Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement and prescription drug coverage relate to one another, and we compare the options available where you live so that your plan reflects your doctors, your prescriptions and your budget.

Beyond health coverage, many of our senior clients want to make thoughtful provision for their families. Final expense coverage and supplemental benefits such as dental, vision and hospital indemnity plans can round out that protection, and we explain each option clearly so that you can choose with confidence and without pressure.

help.heading: How we serve our senior clients

items.title: Unhurried explanation
items.text: We take the time to walk through how each part of Medicare works, and we welcome family members who would like to join the conversation.

items.title: Careful plan comparison
items.text: We review the plans available in your area against your physicians, your prescriptions and your monthly budget before making any recommendation.

items.title: Annual attention
items.text: Plans and needs change from year to year, so we revisit your coverage during each enrollment season to confirm that it still serves you well.

form_intro.heading: Speak with us about your senior benefits
form_intro.text: Tell us a little about your situation, and we will arrange a conversation to review your options with patience and care.

faq.q: When should we begin planning for Medicare?
faq.a: Your Initial Enrollment Period is a seven month window that opens three months before the month you turn sixty five, includes that month, and closes three months after it. Beginning the conversation a few months early leaves time to compare plans against your doctors and prescriptions without the pressure of a deadline.

faq.q: Is there a cost for your guidance?
faq.a: There is no fee for our guidance. We are compensated by the carriers whose plans we place, and the premium for a given plan is the same whether you enroll through us or directly. King Health is not connected with or endorsed by the U.S. government or the federal Medicare program.

faq.q: Does Original Medicare cover dental, vision and hearing?
faq.a: Original Medicare generally does not cover routine dental care, eye examinations for glasses or hearing aids. Standalone ancillary plans, and some Medicare Advantage plans, can close those gaps, and we compare both routes against the care you expect to need.

faq.q: What does final expense insurance provide?
faq.a: Final expense coverage is a modest whole life policy intended to cover funeral costs, outstanding medical bills and other obligations at the end of life. The benefit is paid directly to your beneficiary, and many policies require answers to a short set of health questions rather than a medical examination.

individual-benefits.title: Individual Benefits | King Health
individual-benefits.heading: Individual and family coverage designed around your life
individual-benefits.lede: From health insurance to life insurance and everyday dental and vision care, we help individuals and families assemble protection that is sound, sensible and affordable.
individual-benefits.card_text: Health, life, dental and vision coverage for individuals and families, compared carefully so that it fits the household budget.
overview: Every household carries its own priorities, and the coverage that protects it should reflect them. We help individuals, couples and families compare health plans, select life insurance that provides for the people who depend on them, and add dental, vision and supplemental benefits that make everyday care more manageable.

Our approach begins with listening. Once we understand your family, your income and your goals, we compare options across carriers and present them clearly, so that you can see how each choice affects both your protection and your monthly budget.

help.heading: How we help individuals and families

items.title: A complete picture
items.text: We consider your health coverage, life insurance and supplemental benefits together, so that each part of your plan complements the others.

items.title: Budget conscious guidance
items.text: We look for the combination of coverage and cost that protects your household without asking more of your finances than is comfortable.

items.title: Support as life changes
items.text: Marriage, a new child, a new home or a new career can all call for a fresh look, and we are glad to review your plan whenever your circumstances shift.

form_intro.heading: Speak with us about coverage for your household
form_intro.text: Share a few details about your family and your goals, and we will prepare a thoughtful comparison of the options that suit you.

faq.q: When can we enroll in an individual health plan?
faq.a: Individual health plans generally enroll during the annual Open Enrollment Period each fall. Outside that window, a qualifying life event such as losing employer coverage, marriage, the birth of a child or a move can open a Special Enrollment Period, which is typically limited to sixty days from the event.

faq.q: Should we choose term or whole life insurance?
faq.a: Term life insurance covers a defined period, such as the years a mortgage remains outstanding or children live at home, at a lower premium. Whole life insurance lasts for your lifetime and builds cash value at a higher premium. Many households combine the two, and we model both against your goals before recommending either.

faq.q: How much life insurance does our family need?
faq.a: The right amount depends on the income your household would need to replace, outstanding debts, future obligations such as education, and the savings and coverage you already hold. We work through each of those figures with you rather than relying on a single rule of thumb.

faq.q: Is dedicated dental and vision coverage worth adding?
faq.a: For households that expect regular cleanings, fillings, eye examinations or new lenses, a dedicated dental and vision plan can reduce out of pocket costs considerably. Waiting periods often apply to major dental work, so enrolling before the need arises tends to matter.

group-benefits.title: Group Benefits | King Health
group-benefits.heading: Group benefits that help you care for the people who build your business
group-benefits.lede: We help employers design health, life, dental and vision benefits that attract and retain good people while respecting the realities of a business budget.
group-benefits.card_text: Health, life, dental and vision benefits for employers, designed to support your team and respect your budget.
overview: A thoughtful benefits package is among the most meaningful ways an employer can show care for a team. We work with business owners to understand their workforce, their goals and their budget, and we compare group health, group life, dental, vision and supplemental options so that the program you offer is both valued by employees and sustainable for the business.

We also handle much of the work that makes benefits feel complicated. From gathering census information and presenting proposals to supporting enrollment and answering employee questions, we serve as a steady partner throughout the plan year and at every renewal.

items.title: Benefits shaped to your workforce
items.text: We consider the size, needs and preferences of your team so that the program reflects the people it serves.

items.title: Sensible cost structures
items.text: We explain employer paid and voluntary options clearly, helping you decide how to share costs in a way that works for the business and its employees.

items.title: Enrollment and renewal support
items.text: We guide your employees through enrollment and return each renewal season to review the program, the market and any changes that may serve you better.

form_intro.heading: Speak with us about benefits for your team
form_intro.text: Tell us about your business and your goals for employee benefits, and we will arrange a conversation to explore the options together.

faq.q: Is our business large enough to offer group coverage?
faq.a: Eligibility rules vary by carrier and by state, and many carriers write small group plans for businesses with only a handful of employees. We confirm the participation and eligibility requirements that apply to your company before any quote is prepared.

faq.q: What will group coverage cost the business?
faq.a: Employers typically contribute a share of each employee premium, and carriers often set a minimum employer contribution. We model several contribution levels so that you can see the cost to the business and the cost to employees side by side before you commit.

faq.q: Can we offer dental, vision or life without group health?
faq.a: In many cases you can. Group dental, vision and life plans can often be offered on their own or added later, which allows a business to begin with a focused benefits package and expand it as the team grows.

faq.q: How long does it take for coverage to begin?
faq.a: Group plans usually take effect on the first day of a month once the carrier approves the application, the employee census and the initial premium. Timing depends on underwriting, so we recommend beginning the process several weeks before the date you have in mind.

retirement.title: Retirement | King Health
retirement.heading: Retirement strategies that bring confidence to the years you have worked toward
retirement.lede: We help you consider annuities and indexed universal life as part of a retirement plan built for steady income, careful growth and lasting provision for your family.
retirement.card_text: Annuities and indexed universal life explained clearly, so that your retirement plan supports dependable income and lasting provision.
overview: Retirement is a season to enjoy, and it rests most comfortably on a plan that provides dependable income and preserves what you have built. We help you understand how fixed, fixed indexed and income annuities work, and how indexed universal life can combine permanent protection with the potential for cash value accumulation.

These are long term commitments, so we take care to explain each feature, cost and limitation before you decide. Our role is to help you see how an insurance based strategy may complement your savings, your pension or your other retirement resources, and to recommend only what suits your goals and your comfort.

help.heading: How we guide your retirement planning

items.title: Clarity before commitment
items.text: We explain how crediting, surrender periods, income options and policy charges work, so that you understand every product before you choose it.

items.title: Income you can plan around
items.text: We focus on strategies that can provide steady, predictable income and protect your savings from the swings of the market.

items.title: Provision for those who follow
items.text: We help you consider how your retirement plan can also leave a meaningful legacy for your spouse, your children or the causes you care about.

form_intro.heading: Speak with us about your retirement plan
form_intro.text: Share a few details about your goals for retirement, and we will arrange a conversation to explore the strategies that may suit you.

faq.q: How does an annuity differ from indexed universal life?
faq.a: An annuity is designed primarily to accumulate savings and convert them into dependable income, while indexed universal life is permanent life insurance that provides a death benefit and builds cash value linked to the performance of a market index. Each serves a different purpose, and some plans use both.

faq.q: Can we lose money in an indexed product?
faq.a: Index crediting in fixed indexed annuities and indexed universal life is protected from index declines. Surrender charges, rider fees, policy charges or withdrawals beyond the contract allowance can still reduce the value, so we review those terms carefully before you commit.

faq.q: When should we begin planning for retirement income?
faq.a: Earlier planning allows more time for growth and more flexibility in how income is structured. A review in the years immediately before retirement remains valuable, because it can clarify how guaranteed income, savings and coverage will work together.

faq.q: Do you replace our financial advisor or tax professional?
faq.a: We do not. Our role is the insurance and annuity side of your plan, and we coordinate with your financial advisor and tax professional so that each recommendation fits the strategy you already have in place.

medicare.title: Medicare Guidance | King Health
medicare.heading: Medicare guidance that brings calm to an important decision
medicare.lede: We help you understand your Medicare choices and compare the plans available where you live, so that your coverage reflects your doctors, your prescriptions and your budget.
medicare.card_text: Clear guidance on Original Medicare, Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement and prescription drug plans.
at_a_glance: Medicare is the federal health insurance program for people who qualify by age or by certain disabilities or conditions. Original Medicare consists of Part A, which helps with hospital care, and Part B, which helps with doctor visits, outpatient services and preventive care. Many people pair Original Medicare with a Medicare Supplement plan, which helps with costs that Original Medicare leaves to you, and a Part D plan for prescription drugs.

Medicare Advantage, sometimes called Part C, is an alternative offered by private insurers approved by Medicare. These plans provide the benefits of Part A and Part B, often include prescription drug coverage, and may offer additional benefits such as dental, vision or hearing care, usually within a network of providers. King Health is not connected with or endorsed by the U.S. government or the federal Medicare program. We do not offer every plan available in your area, and you may always contact Medicare directly or visit Medicare.gov for a complete view of your options.
designed_for: This guidance is designed for people approaching Medicare eligibility, those already enrolled who would like to review their coverage, and adult children who are helping a parent make sense of the choices. It is equally suited to someone who is retiring from employer coverage and to someone who simply wants to confirm that the current plan still fits.
how_it_works: We begin by learning about your physicians, your prescriptions, the places you receive care and the budget you are comfortable with. With that understanding, we compare the Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement and prescription drug plans available in your area and explain how each would affect your access to care and your costs throughout the year.

Medicare has defined enrollment periods, including an initial window when you first become eligible, an annual enrollment period each fall when plan changes are permitted, and special enrollment periods triggered by certain life events. We help you understand which window applies to you, complete your enrollment accurately and revisit your plan each year as benefits and needs change.

faq.q: Should we choose Medicare Advantage or a Medicare Supplement plan?
faq.a: Each approach suits different priorities. Medicare Supplement plans pair with Original Medicare and offer broad freedom to see providers who accept Medicare, while Medicare Advantage plans often feature lower monthly premiums and added benefits within a network. We compare these approaches against your doctors, your travel habits and your budget before recommending a direction.

faq.q: Is there a cost for your Medicare guidance?
faq.a: There is no fee for our guidance. We are compensated by the carriers whose plans we place, and the premium for a given plan is the same whether you enroll through us or directly. King Health is not connected with or endorsed by the U.S. government or the federal Medicare program. We do not offer every plan available in your area, and you may always contact Medicare directly or visit Medicare.gov for a complete view of your options.

faq.q: Can we change plans after we enroll?
faq.a: In many cases you can. The annual enrollment period each fall allows changes to Medicare Advantage and prescription drug coverage, and certain life events open special enrollment periods. Changing a Medicare Supplement plan may involve health questions depending on your state and timing, so we review the rules that apply to you before any change.

final-expense.title: Final Expense Insurance | King Health
final-expense.heading: Final expense coverage that lets your family focus on what matters
final-expense.lede: Final expense insurance is a modest whole life policy designed to provide for final arrangements and related costs, giving your loved ones room to gather and remember together.
final-expense.card_text: Modest, permanent life insurance designed to provide for final arrangements so that your family can focus on one another.
at_a_glance: Final expense insurance is a form of whole life insurance with a smaller benefit amount, intended to help with funeral and burial costs, outstanding medical bills and other final arrangements. Because it is permanent coverage, it remains in force for life as long as premiums are paid, and premiums generally stay level for the life of the policy.

The benefit is paid directly to the beneficiaries you name, who may use it in whatever way serves the family best. Many policies also build a modest cash value over time, and benefit amounts, underwriting and features vary by carrier and by state.
designed_for: Final expense coverage is designed for older adults who would like to make thoughtful provision for their families without purchasing a large life insurance policy. It is often a good fit for people on a fixed income, people whose earlier coverage has ended, and people who simply want the reassurance of knowing that final arrangements are already provided for.
how_it_works: Many final expense policies use simplified underwriting, which means acceptance is based on a short set of health questions rather than a medical examination. For applicants with more significant health history, guaranteed acceptance policies are also available, and these typically include a waiting period before the full benefit applies.

We help you choose a benefit amount that reflects your wishes and fits comfortably within your monthly budget, compare carriers whose underwriting suits your health profile, and complete the application with you. Once your policy is in place, we remain available to your family to help them file a claim when the time comes.

faq.q: Will we need a medical examination?
faq.a: Usually not. Most final expense policies rely on health questions alone, and guaranteed acceptance options ask no health questions at all, although those policies generally include a waiting period before the full benefit is available.

faq.q: How do we decide on the right benefit amount?
faq.a: We consider the arrangements you envision, any other coverage or savings you already have and the premium that fits your budget. Our aim is to provide meaningful provision without asking more of your monthly income than is comfortable.

faq.q: Can the benefit be used for expenses other than a funeral?
faq.a: Yes. The benefit is paid to your beneficiaries, who may use it for funeral costs, remaining medical bills, travel for family members or any other need that arises.

ancillary.title: Ancillary Coverage | King Health
ancillary.heading: Ancillary coverage that fills the spaces a primary plan leaves open
ancillary.lede: Dental, vision, hearing, accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity and cancer coverage can strengthen any plan, and we arrange these benefits for seniors, individuals and employers alike.
ancillary.card_text: Supplemental dental, vision, hearing, accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity and cancer coverage that strengthens your primary plan.
at_a_glance: Ancillary coverage refers to supplemental benefits that work alongside your primary health insurance. Dental, vision and hearing plans help with routine and restorative care that medical coverage often excludes, while accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity and cancer policies pay cash benefits directly to you when a covered event occurs, which you may use for deductibles, household bills or any other need.

For seniors, these benefits can complement Original Medicare or a Medicare Supplement plan, neither of which generally includes routine dental, vision or hearing care. For individuals and families, they add a layer of financial steadiness to a health plan. For employers, they offer valued voluntary benefits that employees can elect, often at little or no cost to the business. Availability and benefit design vary by state and by carrier.
designed_for: Ancillary coverage is designed for anyone who would like more complete protection than a primary health plan alone provides. Seniors often add dental, vision and hearing coverage, individuals and families frequently choose accident or hospital indemnity plans to soften unexpected expenses, and employers use these benefits to round out a competitive package without adding substantial cost.
how_it_works: Dental, vision and hearing plans typically pay toward covered services at participating providers, with preventive care often covered most generously and some major services subject to waiting periods. Accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity and cancer plans work differently: when a covered event occurs, the plan pays a set cash benefit directly to you, regardless of what your health insurance pays.

We begin by reviewing the coverage you already have and identifying where supplemental benefits would provide the most value for the premium. For employers, we design voluntary offerings that employees can elect through payroll deduction. In every case, we compare carriers and benefit levels so that the protection you add is both useful and affordable.

faq.q: Do these plans replace our health insurance?
faq.a: No. Ancillary plans are designed to supplement your primary coverage rather than replace it. They fill specific needs such as routine dental care or provide cash benefits that help with costs your health plan does not cover.

faq.q: Can we purchase ancillary coverage on its own?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. Seniors, individuals and families can usually purchase these plans individually, and employers can offer them to their teams as part of a group or voluntary benefits program.

faq.q: How are cash benefits paid?
faq.a: Accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity and cancer plans generally pay benefits directly to you once a covered claim is approved. The funds are yours to use as you see fit, whether for medical bills, travel, childcare or everyday household expenses.

individual-health.title: Individual Health Insurance | King Health
individual-health.heading: Individual health coverage chosen with care for you and your family
individual-health.lede: We compare marketplace and private health plans so that you can choose coverage that protects your household and fits comfortably within your budget.
individual-health.card_text: Marketplace and private health plans for individuals and families, compared carefully for value and fit.
at_a_glance: Individual health insurance covers people who do not receive coverage through an employer or a government program. Plans offered through the health insurance marketplace include essential health benefits such as preventive care, hospital care and prescription drugs, and they cannot deny coverage or charge more because of existing health conditions. Depending on household income, you may qualify for premium tax credits that reduce your monthly cost.

Private plans purchased outside the marketplace are also available, and some offer different network or pricing structures that may suit particular circumstances. Because the rules, benefits and protections differ between plan types, and because availability varies by state and by carrier, we explain each option clearly before you decide.
designed_for: Individual health coverage is designed for people who are self employed, own a small business without a group plan, work for an employer that does not offer coverage, are between positions or are retiring before Medicare eligibility. It also serves families who would like to compare their employer plan against what the individual market can offer.
how_it_works: We begin by understanding your household, your preferred doctors and hospitals, your prescriptions and your budget. We then compare the plans available in your area, explaining how premiums, deductibles, copays and networks interact so that you can see the full cost of each option rather than the monthly premium alone.

Marketplace plans may be purchased during the annual open enrollment period or during a special enrollment period that follows a qualifying life event, such as a move, a marriage, the birth of a child or the loss of other coverage. We help you determine your eligibility for savings, complete your enrollment and review your plan each year.

faq.q: Can we qualify for help with the cost of coverage?
faq.a: Many households do. Premium tax credits for marketplace plans are based on household income and size, and we will help you estimate whether you qualify and how much the credit may reduce your premium.

faq.q: What if we need coverage outside the open enrollment period?
faq.a: A qualifying life event such as a move, a marriage, a new child or the loss of other coverage may open a special enrollment period. Some private plans also accept applications throughout the year, and we will review which options are available to you.

faq.q: Will our current doctors be in network?
faq.a: Networks vary from plan to plan, so we check your preferred physicians and hospitals against each option before making a recommendation.

whole-life.title: Whole Life Insurance | King Health
whole-life.heading: Whole life insurance that provides for your family for a lifetime
whole-life.lede: Whole life insurance offers permanent protection, level premiums and guaranteed cash value growth, creating a foundation your family can rely on.
whole-life.card_text: Permanent protection with level premiums and guaranteed cash value growth, built to last a lifetime.
at_a_glance: Whole life insurance is permanent coverage that remains in force for your entire life as long as premiums are paid. Premiums are generally level, which means they do not increase as you grow older, and the death benefit is paid to your beneficiaries income tax free in most circumstances.

Each policy also builds cash value at a guaranteed rate over time. Some whole life policies issued by mutual companies may also earn dividends, although dividends are not guaranteed. The cash value grows on a tax deferred basis and may be accessed through policy loans or withdrawals, which reduce the death benefit if they are not repaid.
designed_for: Whole life insurance is designed for people who want protection that never expires, such as parents who wish to leave a lasting inheritance, business owners planning for succession, and anyone who values the predictability of level premiums and guaranteed cash value. It is also well suited to families who would like to provide for a loved one with lifelong needs.
how_it_works: When you purchase a whole life policy, you select a death benefit and pay a level premium for the life of the policy or for a defined payment period. A portion of each premium supports the cost of insurance, and the remainder contributes to the cash value, which grows steadily according to the guarantees in your contract.

We compare whole life policies across carriers, considering the strength of each company, the guaranteed values, any dividend history and the premium that fits your budget. We then help you through underwriting and remain available to review your policy, beneficiaries and cash value as your life unfolds.

faq.q: How does whole life differ from term life?
faq.a: Term life covers a defined period and generally carries a lower premium, while whole life covers your entire lifetime and builds cash value. Many families combine these forms of coverage, and we help you decide which approach, or which combination, best fits your goals and your budget.

faq.q: Can we use the cash value during our lifetime?
faq.a: Yes. You may borrow against the cash value or make withdrawals, subject to your policy terms. Outstanding loans and withdrawals reduce the death benefit, so we review the effect of any access with you beforehand.

faq.q: Will our premium ever increase?
faq.a: Traditional whole life policies carry a level premium that is set when the policy is issued and does not rise with age.

term-life.title: Term Life Insurance | King Health
term-life.heading: Term life insurance that protects your family through the years that matter most
term-life.lede: Term life insurance provides substantial protection for a defined period at an accessible cost, helping your family stay secure while they depend on your income.
term-life.card_text: Substantial, affordable protection for the years when your family depends most on your income.
at_a_glance: Term life insurance provides a death benefit for a defined period, often chosen to match the years of a mortgage, the years until children are grown or the years remaining until retirement. Premiums generally remain level throughout the term, and because the coverage is temporary, term life typically offers the most protection for the lowest premium.

Many term policies include a conversion option that allows you to exchange some or all of the coverage for a permanent policy without new medical underwriting, within the limits your contract sets. Some policies are also renewable at the end of the term, usually at a higher premium. Features and availability vary by carrier and by state.
designed_for: Term life insurance is designed for people whose families rely on their income, including young parents, homeowners with a mortgage, couples planning for the future and business owners who want to protect a partner or a loan. It is especially valuable when a household needs a meaningful amount of protection at a premium that fits a growing family budget.
how_it_works: You select a coverage amount and a term length that reflect your family's needs, and you pay a level premium for the duration of the term. If you pass away while the policy is in force, your beneficiaries receive the death benefit, generally free of income tax, to replace your income, pay off debts or fund future goals.

We help you determine an appropriate amount of coverage by considering your income, your debts and the goals you hold for your family. We then compare carriers whose underwriting suits your health profile, guide you through the application and remind you of conversion opportunities as the end of your term approaches.

faq.q: How much coverage does our family need?
faq.a: The right amount depends on your income, your debts, your children's future needs and the savings you already have. We work through these factors with you and recommend a figure that provides meaningful protection at a premium you can sustain.

faq.q: What happens when the term ends?
faq.a: Depending on your policy, you may convert some or all of the coverage to a permanent policy, renew it at a higher premium, or allow it to end if your family no longer needs it. We review these choices with you well before the term concludes.

faq.q: Is a medical examination required?
faq.a: Some policies require a brief examination, while others rely on health questions and records alone. We will explain the underwriting path for each carrier we recommend.

dental-vision.title: Dental and Vision Insurance | King Health
dental-vision.heading: Dental and vision coverage that keeps everyday care within reach
dental-vision.lede: Individual dental and vision plans help you and your family maintain healthy smiles and clear sight with predictable, manageable costs.
dental-vision.card_text: Individual and family dental and vision plans that make routine care predictable and affordable.
at_a_glance: Individual dental insurance generally covers preventive care such as cleanings and examinations most generously, with basic services such as fillings and major services such as crowns or bridges covered at progressively lower levels. Many plans include an annual maximum benefit and a waiting period before major services are covered.

Individual vision insurance typically helps with routine eye examinations and provides an allowance toward eyeglass frames, lenses or contact lenses. Dental and vision plans may be purchased separately or together, and benefits, networks and waiting periods vary by carrier and by state.
designed_for: These plans are designed for individuals and families who do not have dental or vision benefits through an employer, retirees whose health plan does not include routine dental or vision care, and anyone who would like to budget for these services with greater predictability.
how_it_works: You pay a monthly premium, and the plan pays a share of the cost of covered services, usually with the greatest savings when you visit providers within the plan's network. Some plans allow you to see any dentist or eye doctor, while others offer lower premiums in exchange for a defined network.

We compare plans by looking at your current dentist and eye doctor, the services you anticipate and the premium that fits your budget. If you are planning significant dental work, we pay close attention to waiting periods and annual maximums so that your plan serves you when you need it.

faq.q: Are there waiting periods before coverage begins?
faq.a: Preventive care is often covered right away, while basic and major services may carry waiting periods. Some plans waive these waiting periods for applicants with prior dental coverage, and we will point out those options where they are available.

faq.q: Can we keep our current dentist?
faq.a: In many cases you can. We check whether your dentist and eye doctor participate in each plan's network, and we also identify plans that allow you to visit any provider.

faq.q: Should we purchase dental and vision together?
faq.a: Bundling is often convenient and can be cost effective, but it is not required. We compare stand alone and combined plans so that you pay only for the coverage your family will use.

group-health.title: Group Health Insurance | King Health
group-health.heading: Group health insurance that supports your team and sustains your business
group-health.lede: We help employers select group health plans that provide valued coverage for employees and their families while keeping costs predictable for the business.
group-health.card_text: Employer sponsored health plans designed to care for your team and keep business costs predictable.
at_a_glance: Group health insurance is coverage an employer purchases for eligible employees and, often, their dependents. The employer typically contributes toward the premium, and employee contributions are usually made through payroll deduction on a pretax basis. Group plans generally offer broader benefits and more favorable rates than comparable individual coverage.

Employers may choose among several funding arrangements, including fully insured plans, level funded plans and health reimbursement arrangements, each with its own balance of predictability and flexibility. Eligibility, participation requirements and plan designs vary by carrier and by state, and we explain each option in plain terms.
designed_for: Group health coverage is designed for small and growing businesses that want to attract and retain capable people, owners who would like to provide for their own families through the business, and established employers who would like to review their current program at renewal.
how_it_works: We begin by learning about your workforce, your current benefits if any and the budget you have in mind. We gather the census information carriers require, request proposals across the market and present a clear comparison of plan designs, networks and employer and employee costs.

Once you select a program, we coordinate enrollment, help your employees understand their choices and serve as their point of contact for questions throughout the year. At each renewal, we review your program against the market and recommend adjustments that keep it valuable and sustainable.

faq.q: How small can a business be to offer group health coverage?
faq.a: Many carriers offer group plans to quite small businesses, including some with only a few employees. Minimum participation and contribution requirements vary by carrier and by state, and we will confirm what applies to your business.

faq.q: How much must the employer contribute?
faq.a: Carriers typically require a minimum employer contribution toward employee coverage, and employers may choose to contribute more or to help with dependent coverage. We help you design a contribution strategy that fits your budget and your goals for the team.

faq.q: Can we offer employees a choice among plan options?
faq.a: Many carriers allow employers to offer a choice of plans, which lets employees select the balance of premium and benefits that suits their own households. We will show you which arrangements are available.

group-life.title: Group Life Insurance | King Health
group-life.heading: Group life insurance that extends your care to your employees' families
group-life.lede: Group life insurance gives employees valued protection for their loved ones and gives employers an efficient way to strengthen their benefits program.
group-life.card_text: Employer paid and voluntary life insurance that extends meaningful protection to your employees' families.
at_a_glance: Group life insurance is term life coverage provided through an employer. Basic group life is often paid by the employer and may be offered as a flat amount or as a multiple of salary, while voluntary or supplemental group life allows employees to purchase additional coverage for themselves and often for a spouse or children through payroll deduction.

Group life is frequently paired with accidental death and dismemberment coverage, and many policies allow employees to continue or convert their coverage if they leave the company. Because enrollment is offered to the group, employees can often obtain a meaningful amount of coverage with simplified underwriting. Features and limits vary by carrier.
designed_for: Group life insurance is designed for employers of every size who would like to offer a benefit that employees value highly at a modest cost to the business. It is particularly meaningful for teams with young families and for employers who want to complement a group health plan with broader protection.
how_it_works: We help you decide on the structure of the basic benefit, whether to offer voluntary coverage and how the program should interact with your other benefits. We then compare carriers, coordinate enrollment and explain the coverage to your employees in clear terms so that they understand what they have.
Throughout the year, we support you with additions, changes and claims, and we review the program at renewal so that it remains competitive and continues to meet the needs of your team.

faq.q: Is employer paid group life taxable to employees?
faq.a: Employer paid group term life coverage above a certain amount may create imputed income for employees under federal tax rules. We explain how this works and coordinate with your payroll provider so that it is handled correctly.

faq.q: Can employees keep their coverage if they leave?
faq.a: Many group life policies include portability or conversion provisions that allow departing employees to continue coverage on an individual basis. The specific terms depend on the carrier and the policy.

faq.q: Do employees need to answer health questions?
faq.a: Basic coverage and amounts of voluntary coverage up to a guaranteed issue limit often require no health questions when elected during initial enrollment. Larger amounts may require evidence of insurability.

group-ancillary.title: Group Ancillary Benefits | King Health
group-ancillary.heading: Group ancillary benefits that round out the package your team relies on
group-ancillary.lede: Accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity, cancer and disability coverage offered through the workplace, so your employees gain added protection and your business strengthens its benefits without carrying the full cost.
group-ancillary.card_text: Workplace accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity, cancer and disability coverage that employers can offer on an employer paid or voluntary basis.
at_a_glance: Group ancillary benefits are supplemental coverages offered through an employer alongside the core group health plan. They commonly include accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity and cancer insurance, which pay cash benefits directly to the employee when a covered event occurs, as well as short term and long term disability coverage, which replaces a portion of income when an illness or injury keeps an employee from working. These plans provide limited benefits and do not replace comprehensive health insurance.

Unlike an individually purchased policy, a group plan is arranged under a master contract held by the employer. Benefits can be fully employer paid, shared between the business and its employees, or offered on a voluntary basis in which employees pay their own premiums through payroll deduction, so a business can expand its package with little or no added cost. Plan design, eligibility and pricing are set at the group level and vary by carrier and by state.
designed_for: Group ancillary benefits are designed for employers of every size who want to strengthen recruiting and retention, give employees choices that fit their own households, and help their teams manage the deductibles and out of pocket costs that higher deductible health plans can bring. Accident coverage often suits physical and hourly workforces, while critical illness, hospital indemnity and disability coverage appeal broadly to employees who want a financial cushion when life is interrupted.
how_it_works: Most group ancillary plans are offered during an enrollment period, when eligible employees can elect coverage for themselves and often for a spouse and children. Many carriers offer guaranteed issue or simplified enrollment at that time, which means coverage up to set limits can be issued without a medical exam, and carriers typically require a minimum level of participation before a plan can be placed.

When a covered event occurs, cash benefit plans pay a set amount directly to the employee, regardless of what the health plan pays, and disability plans pay a portion of the employee's earnings for a defined period after a waiting period. Some policies allow employees to keep their coverage if they leave the company while others end with employment, so we review portability, participation rules and contribution options with you, compare carriers side by side and help you plan an enrollment your team understands.

faq.q: Who pays for group ancillary benefits?
faq.a: The employer decides. Benefits can be fully employer paid, shared between the business and its employees, or offered on a voluntary basis in which employees pay their own premiums through payroll deduction, which adds valuable choices at little or no cost to the business.

faq.q: How is this different from ancillary coverage purchased individually?
faq.a: Group ancillary coverage is arranged through the employer under a group contract, with eligibility, plan design and pricing set for the whole group, and enrollment usually takes place during a set enrollment period. Individual ancillary policies are purchased and owned directly by the policyholder, with underwriting and pricing determined individually.

faq.q: Do employees need a medical exam to enroll?
faq.a: Often they do not. Many carriers offer guaranteed issue or simplified enrollment during the initial enrollment period, up to set coverage limits. Requirements vary by carrier, product and group size, and enrolling after that window may require answers to health questions.

faq.q: Can employees keep coverage if they leave the company?
faq.a: It depends on the plan. Some group policies include a portability or conversion option that lets a departing employee continue coverage by paying the carrier directly, while others end when employment ends. We confirm these terms before you choose a plan.

faq.q: Is there a minimum number of participants?
faq.a: Carriers commonly require a minimum level of participation for a group ancillary plan to be placed and renewed, and the threshold usually differs between employer paid and voluntary plans. We confirm the requirements that apply to your company before any quote is prepared.

group-dental-vision.title: Group Dental and Vision Insurance | King Health
group-dental-vision.heading: Group dental and vision benefits your employees will use and appreciate
group-dental-vision.lede: Group dental and vision plans are among the most valued and most frequently used employee benefits, and we help employers offer them in a way that suits the budget.
group-dental-vision.card_text: Employer paid or voluntary dental and vision plans that your team will use and appreciate.
at_a_glance: Group dental plans generally cover preventive care such as cleanings and examinations most generously, with basic and major services covered at progressively lower levels up to an annual maximum. Group vision plans typically cover routine eye examinations and provide allowances toward frames, lenses or contact lenses.

Employers may pay for these benefits in full, share the cost with employees or offer them on a voluntary basis that employees fund through payroll deduction. Group plans often feature richer benefits and shorter waiting periods than comparable individual plans, and designs vary by carrier and by state.
designed_for: Group dental and vision coverage is designed for employers who want to round out a health plan with benefits employees use throughout the year, and for businesses that would like to offer meaningful benefits on a voluntary basis even before introducing a group health plan.
how_it_works: We review your team's needs and your budget, then compare plan designs, networks and funding options across carriers. Whether you choose an employer paid, contributory or voluntary approach, we present the options clearly so that you can see how each would serve your employees.

We coordinate enrollment, help employees confirm that their dentists and eye doctors participate, and remain available for questions throughout the year. At renewal, we review usage and pricing to keep the program valuable and sustainable.

faq.q: Can we offer these benefits without paying for them?
faq.a: Yes. Voluntary dental and vision plans allow employees to purchase coverage at group rates through payroll deduction, often with minimal administrative effort for the employer.

faq.q: Are there participation requirements?
faq.a: Many carriers set minimum participation levels, particularly for employer paid plans. We will confirm the requirements for each option and help you choose a structure that your team will support.

faq.q: Do group plans have waiting periods?
faq.a: Waiting periods for major services are common, but group plans frequently shorten or waive them, especially for larger groups or employer paid programs. We compare these terms as part of our recommendation.

annuities.title: Annuities | King Health
annuities.heading: Annuities that turn your savings into dependable retirement income
annuities.lede: Fixed, fixed indexed and income annuities can protect your savings, grow on a tax deferred basis and provide income you can rely on for as long as you live.
annuities.card_text: Fixed, fixed indexed and income annuities designed to protect savings and provide dependable retirement income.
at_a_glance: An annuity is a contract with an insurance company in which you make a lump sum payment or a series of payments, and the company agrees to credit interest and, when you choose, to provide income. Fixed annuities credit a declared interest rate for a set period. Fixed indexed annuities credit interest based in part on the performance of a market index, subject to a cap or participation rate, while protecting your principal from index declines. Income annuities convert a sum of money into a stream of payments that may begin right away or at a future date and may last for life.

Earnings within an annuity grow tax deferred until withdrawn. Annuities are long term products, and most include a surrender period during which withdrawals above a certain amount incur charges; withdrawals may also be subject to income tax and, depending on your age, a federal tax penalty. Annuities are not bank deposits and are not insured by the FDIC, and their guarantees are backed by the claims paying ability of the issuing insurer.
designed_for: Annuities are designed for people approaching or enjoying retirement who would like to protect a portion of their savings from market declines, create a dependable income stream to cover essential expenses, or accumulate savings on a tax deferred basis beyond what employer plans and individual retirement accounts allow.
how_it_works: Most annuities have an accumulation phase, during which your money earns interest according to the contract, and an income phase, during which the annuity pays you. Some contracts allow you to add an income rider that provides lifetime withdrawals regardless of the account value, typically for an additional cost.

We begin by understanding your income needs, your other resources, your time horizon and your comfort with tradeoffs between growth, guarantees and access. We then compare contracts across carriers, explaining crediting methods, surrender schedules, fees and income options in plain language, and recommend a contract only when it suits your goals.

faq.q: Can we lose money in a fixed indexed annuity?
faq.a: The principal and credited interest in a fixed indexed annuity are protected from index declines. However, surrender charges, optional rider fees or withdrawals beyond the contract allowance can reduce the value, so we review these terms carefully before you commit.

faq.q: Can we access our money if we need it?
faq.a: Most annuities allow a portion of the value to be withdrawn each year without a surrender charge, and many waive charges in certain circumstances such as confinement to a nursing facility. Larger withdrawals during the surrender period may incur charges and taxes, which we explain fully.

faq.q: How is annuity income taxed?
faq.a: Earnings are taxed as ordinary income when withdrawn, and the treatment of income payments depends on how the annuity was funded. We recommend consulting your tax professional, and we are glad to coordinate with them.

indexed-universal-life.title: Indexed Universal Life | King Health
indexed-universal-life.heading: Indexed universal life that combines lasting protection with the potential for growth
indexed-universal-life.lede: Indexed universal life provides permanent coverage and cash value that can grow with a market index, protected by a floor and moderated by a cap.
indexed-universal-life.card_text: Permanent life insurance with flexible premiums and cash value credited from a market index, protected by a floor.
at_a_glance: Indexed universal life is permanent life insurance that pairs a death benefit with a cash value account. The cash value earns interest credited from the performance of a market index, such as a broad stock index, without being directly invested in the market. A floor protects the cash value from losses when the index declines, while a cap or participation rate limits the amount of interest credited in strong years.

Premiums are flexible within the limits of the policy, and the cash value grows on a tax deferred basis. It may be accessed through policy loans or withdrawals, which reduce the death benefit and the cash value if they are not repaid. Policy charges continue to apply each year regardless of index performance, and caps, floors, participation rates and riders vary by carrier and by product.
designed_for: Indexed universal life is designed for people who want lifelong protection for their families along with the potential to build cash value that may supplement retirement income. It is often considered by established professionals, business owners and families who have already funded their employer retirement plans and would like an additional tax advantaged resource.
how_it_works: Each premium you pay, after policy charges, is added to the cash value, which you may allocate between a fixed account and index accounts. At the end of each crediting period, interest is credited based on the index performance, never less than the floor and never more than the cap. Over time, this structure is designed to capture a portion of market growth while protecting the account from market losses.

Because indexed universal life is a long term strategy, careful design and consistent funding are essential to keeping the policy in force as intended. We illustrate how the policy may perform under a range of assumptions, explain every charge and feature clearly and review the policy with you regularly so that it stays aligned with your goals.

faq.q: Is our cash value invested in the stock market?
faq.a: No. Interest is credited based on the performance of an index, but your cash value is not invested directly in the market. This is what allows the floor to protect your account from index losses.

faq.q: How can indexed universal life support retirement?
faq.a: Once sufficient cash value has accumulated, you may access it through policy loans or withdrawals to supplement retirement income. Because access affects the death benefit and the long term health of the policy, we plan these distributions carefully with you.

faq.q: Are the illustrated values guaranteed?
faq.a: Illustrations show how a policy may perform under stated assumptions, and actual results will vary with index performance and policy charges. We review the guaranteed values alongside the illustrated values so that you understand the full range of outcomes.

about.mission: At King Health, we care for the people we serve the way they care for the people they love. Every family deserves the quiet confidence of knowing that those they cherish will be provided for, and we hold that trust as a privilege rather than a transaction. We listen before we recommend, we compare with diligence so that protection fits the budget as faithfully as it fits the need, and we remain beside our clients long after the paperwork is signed. story: Javon King founded King Health because he saw how often families made important coverage decisions without anyone taking the time to explain their choices or to look for an option they could comfortably afford. He built the advisory to offer something better: patient, personal counsel from someone who cares about a client's loved ones as much as the client does.

Today Javon leads King Health as its founder and principal advisor. He and our team work with seniors navigating Medicare, families protecting their futures, employers caring for their teams and retirees seeking dependable income. In every conversation, the commitment is the same: to understand what matters most to you, to compare your options with care and to recommend only what serves you well.

posts.title: How the autumn Medicare enrollment window works
posts.summary: Each autumn, Medicare opens a window in which beneficiaries may review their coverage and change plans for the coming year. Understanding what can change, and what your plan's annual notice tells you, makes that review far less stressful.

body.text: Medicare coverage is not a decision made once and then forgotten. Plans change their premiums, their networks and the medications they cover from one year to the next, and each autumn Medicare sets aside a period in which beneficiaries may respond to those changes.
What may change during the autumn window

During this period you may move from Original Medicare to a Medicare Advantage plan, return from Medicare Advantage to Original Medicare, switch from one Medicare Advantage plan to another, or join, change or drop a prescription drug plan. Any change you make takes effect at the start of the new year.

Before the window opens, your plan sends an Annual Notice of Change describing what will differ next year. It is easy to set aside, yet it is the single most useful document in the review, because it shows whether your doctors, your pharmacy and your prescriptions will be treated the same way.

items: Review your plan's annual notice as soon as it arrives.
Confirm that your doctors and pharmacy remain in network.
Compare the total yearly cost of your medications, not only the premium.
Remember that a change takes effect at the start of the new year.

body.text: A second opportunity early in the year

Those enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan also have a separate window early in the year in which they may make one change, either to another Medicare Advantage plan or back to Original Medicare. It is a useful safeguard if a new plan does not serve you as expected.

We compare the plans we offer in your area side by side, review your medications and providers with you, and explain the tradeoffs plainly, so that the plan you choose suits the year ahead rather than the year behind.
